repos.title: Which repositories?

repos.not_in_app_single: not in the GitHub App: one at a time only
repos.org_count_error: Couldn't count the repositories in {{name}}. Try again in a moment.
repos.org_none: None of that organization's repositories are in the GitHub App.
repos.batch_note: They run one after another. Follow them in Scans.
repos.not_in_app: {{names}} can't join a batch: only GitHub App repositories can.
repos.over_limit: Up to {{limit}} by hand. For more, choose the whole organization.
repos.batch_busy: Another batch is running. You can still scan one repository.

images.title: Which images?
images.label: One reference per line
images.invalid: These don't look like image references (registry/repository:tag, lowercase): <mono>{{names}}</mono>
images.batch_note: They run one after another. Follow them in Scans.
images.pin_hint: Tip: pin a version or digest so you know exactly what you reviewed.

context.title: Anything the report should say?
context.label: What it does and what worries you most
context.placeholder: Stack, how users sign in, sensitive data it handles…
context.help: Shown in the report as your team's note.

target.title: Which site or API?
target.empty: Add a domain you control and verify it to scan it.

scope.invalid: {{host}} isn't a host name. Use name.example.com or *.example.com.
scope.already_root: That's the domain itself: it's always in scope.
scope.too_many: Up to {{max}} extra hosts per scan.
scope.exact_only: Only {{host}} is covered. Verify by DNS to add subdomains.

spec.title: API documentation
spec.nudge: An API has few links to follow: add its OpenAPI spec so the scan calls each documented endpoint.
spec.instead: With it, the scan also calls every documented endpoint, besides crawling the site.
spec.url_file_loaded: Remove the file to use a URL.
spec.invalid: That file isn't an OpenAPI 2 or 3 spec.
spec.url_foreign: The URL must use HTTPS on {{host}} or a host in scope.

access.title: Does it need a login?
access.text: A token, API key or session cookie, sent as a header.
access.test_account: It browses as that user: use a test account.

access.title: Scan without signing in?
access.text: Only what's public will be covered.

review.title: Ready to launch
review.plan_failed: Couldn't read the repository; the server decides when it runs.

looks.generic: Each repository's code, secrets, dependencies and infrastructure

review.osv_hint: Sends package names and versions (not code) to api.osv.dev. Off: dependencies aren't checked.
review.batch_note: Runs as a batch you can follow and cancel in Scans.
review.schedule_without_spec: Weekly scans browse the site; they don't use the API documentation.
review.waf_text: Allow this server's public IP, or the scan may be blocked.
review.authorization: It only browses and reads, never attacks. Launch it only against sites you're allowed to test.

details.title: Technical details
details.code_generic: Each repository gets its own plan from its real tree: SAST for the languages it has, secrets, dependencies, infrastructure and CI/CD.
details.batch: One at a time and only when nothing else is scanning. What's done is kept if you cancel.

image_runs.packages: System and application packages with Trivy and Grype; advisories both of them report are flagged
image_runs.secrets: Secrets in the layers, the environment variables (ENV) and the build history (ARG, URLs with credentials)
image_runs.config: Configuration: root user, HEALTHCHECK, ADD from a URL, exposed SSH, image age
image_runs.checkov: Checkov on the Dockerfile rebuilt from the history: downloads without TLS verification, unsigned package managers…
image_runs.priority: Priority from CVSS, CISA KEV and EPSS

image_skips.run: The image is never run or built
image_skips.source: The source code that produced it isn't scanned (run a code scan on its repository)
image_skips.secrets: No secret value that turns up is stored, only where it was found

org.estimate_one: {{count}} repository · estimated time {{duration}} (about 1 min per repository; it adjusts to how long they actually take).
org.estimate_other: {{count}} repositories · estimated time {{duration}} (about 1 min per repository; it adjusts to how long they actually take).
org.dialog_description: All its repositories are scanned (except archived ones), one at a time and only when nothing else is scanning, so your own scans and PR reviews never wait. You can keep using the panel and cancel it whenever you like.

batch.confirm_cancel: Whatever is already scanned is kept, and the scan in progress finishes.
batch.progress: {{done}} of {{total}} scanned{{failed}} · {{critical}} critical and {{high}} high so far · {{duration}} left. It moves forward whenever nothing else is scanning, so you can keep using the panel.

import.title: Import SARIF
import.description: Findings from another tool, added to an asset Pitangus already knows. Each tool in the file becomes its own run.
import.asset_error: Couldn't load the assets. Reload the page to try again.
import.no_asset: There are no assets yet: scan a repository or an image first, then import its SARIF.

file.label: SARIF file
file.too_large: {{name}} is {{size}}, over the {{max}} MB limit. Split it by tool or by module and import each part as partial.
file.not_sarif: {{name}} doesn't look like SARIF: it has no runs.

scope.label: Scope
scope.full_hint: Everything the tool checked in this asset: what it no longer reports is marked fixed
scope.partial_hint: Only some files or one module: adds and updates, never marks anything fixed
scope.note: Pitangus scans never close imported findings, and imports never close theirs.

import.tool_hint: Replaces the name in the file.
import.commit_invalid: Use the commit SHA: 7 to 64 hexadecimal characters.
import.branch_invalid: That isn't a valid branch name.
import.too_large: The file is over the server's {{max}} MB limit.

result.title: Imported into {{name}}
result.description_full: One run per tool. Whatever each tool no longer reports is now marked fixed.
result.description_partial: One run per tool. Partial import: nothing was marked fixed.

list.empty_text: Your scans will show up here. Run the first one on a repository or a container image.
list.trigger_advisories: · automatic: published after the last scan
